points.description: Purpose: both RPF and RPB implement broadcasting that is more efficient than flooding, i.e. they minimise the number of duplicate packets in the network during broadcast.
points.partial_credit: Half if only says 'broadcast' or 'efficient' without reference to reducing duplicate packets / improvement over flooding.

points.description: RPF basis: each node uses its routing table from unicast routing algorithms; on receiving a packet from sender S via neighbour N at node X, X checks the routing table for the route to S.
points.partial_credit: Half if routing table is mentioned but the check of the route towards source S via incoming neighbour N is not stated.

points.description: RPF forwarding rule: X forwards the packet to all adjacent nodes except N only if it would itself send packets to S via N (packet arrived on the best/shortest path); otherwise it discards it. Assumption: the packet has used the best route so far.
points.partial_credit: Half if only the forward-if-from-best-path condition is stated, without excluding N or the discard/assumption.

points.description: RPB learning: nodes monitor unicast traffic to learn which paths they lie on; node X knows it is on the best path between A and B if it sees unicast packets from A to B (or vice versa), so each node knows which spanning trees it is part of.
points.partial_credit: Half if only says nodes learn spanning-tree membership without stating that it is by observing unicast traffic.

points.description: RPB forwarding: works identically to RPF, except that it forwards packets only on edges that are part of a spanning tree (still excluding the incoming line N).
points.partial_credit: Half if says it restricts forwarding to spanning-tree edges but not that the rest is the same as RPF/excludes N.

rubric.notes: Full marks need every element stated precisely with correct terms: duplicate-packet reduction versus flooding, the RPF routing-table check via the incoming neighbour N, the forward-to-all-except-N rule, RPB's learning from unicast traffic, and forwarding only on spanning-tree edges. Give part marks only where clearly more than half of a point is precise. A wrong statement (e.g. RPF forwards when the packet did not come from the best route, or RPB uses no spanning tree) or vague generic wording earns nothing for that point.
